sequence_description: I1 issuer mismatch: compare default (no issuer pin) vs pinned issuer config; wrong Issuer should be rejected when pinned, and ideally also rejected by default if issuer checks are enforced.
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML login with a wrong Issuer appears to return HTTP 200/success under default (no issuer pin), but no session is established, suggesting the test may be misclassifying an error page as a successful login rather than a true issuer-validation bypass.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SAML login with a wrong Issuer appears to return HTTP 200/success under default (no issuer pin), but no session is established, suggesting the test may be misclassifying an error page as a successful login rather than a true issuer-validation bypass.

sequence_description: Replay a SAML assertion containing <OneTimeUse/> with the same Assertion/@ID; second login must be rejected.
description: [LLM-Judge] Both the initial and replayed SAML logins returned HTTP 200/success=True, but neither resulted in an authenticated session (verify_granted_identity returned 401), so the test did not actually validate OneTimeUse replay protection and may indicate the SAML flow is not establishing a session.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Both the initial and replayed SAML logins returned HTTP 200/success=True, but neither resulted in an authenticated session (verify_granted_identity returned 401), so the test did not actually validate OneTimeUse replay protection and may indicate the SAML flow is not establishing a session.

description: [LLM-Judge] The IdP was not actually disabled/updated (admin update returned 409 Already exists), so the test’s “login must be rejected after disable” condition was never exercised; the second SAML login succeeding is therefore inconclusive rather than a clear bypass.
